name: Dathan
overview: Dathan was a male member of the tribe of Reuben known primarily for his rebellion against Moses alongside Korah. He is noted in Scripture as a figure of dissent during a critical moment of Israelite history. No additional personal notes are recorded beyond his role in this rebellion.
namesAndTitles: The name Dathan means 'strong,' reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew text. This name does not appear to be divinely given but simply identifies him in the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Dathan was the son of Eliab. Beyond this explicit relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Dathan's significance lies in his participation in the rebellion against Moses, which highlights a challenge to divinely appointed leadership. His actions alongside Korah illustrate the dangers of dissent within God's chosen people and serve as a cautionary example in the biblical account. This episode underscores the importance of obedience to God’s ordained authority.
